CalHFA and Down Payment Assistance in Southern California: A Complete Guide for First-Time Buyers

The State and Local Programs That Can Make Your Down Payment Much More Manageable

By Rudy Corona · February 3, 2026

The Down Payment Problem in Southern California

The biggest barrier for first-time buyers in SoCal is not qualifying for a mortgage — it is coming up with the down payment and closing costs in one of the most expensive housing markets in the country. California has created some of the most comprehensive down payment assistance programs in the nation through the California Housing Finance Agency (CalHFA) and county and city programs layered on top. Most people either do not know these programs exist or assume they will not qualify. Here is what is available.

CalHFA MyHome Assistance Program

CalHFA MyHome is the foundation of California's first-time buyer assistance. It is a deferred-payment junior loan: you borrow for down payment and closing costs, and you do not make monthly payments. The balance is repaid when you sell, refinance, or pay off your first mortgage.

  • Assistance amount: Up to 3% to 3.5% of the purchase price (depending on first loan)
  • Payment: Deferred; no monthly payments until sale, refinance, or first mortgage payoff
  • First loan: Must be paired with a CalHFA-approved first mortgage (CalHFA FHA or CalHFA Conventional)
  • First-time buyer: Yes (no owned/occupied primary in past 3 years)
  • Income & price limits: Vary by county; in SoCal often $180K–$300K+ income and $800K–$1.1M+ purchase price
  • Homebuyer education: Required; HUD-approved course before close

On a $650,000 home with 3.5% MyHome, the state could contribute $22,750 toward your down payment and closing costs. That money sits as a quiet second loan with no monthly payment until you sell or refinance. For many buyers, this closes the gap entirely.

CalHFA Dream For All Shared Appreciation Loan

Dream For All is CalHFA's most powerful program but the most limited in availability — it runs in funding cycles and money goes quickly.

  • Assistance: Up to 20% of the purchase price
  • Repayment: Deferred until sale or refinance; CalHFA receives a proportional share of the home's appreciation when repaid
  • First-generation: At least one borrower must be a first-generation homebuyer (parents did not own in the U.S.)
  • First-time buyer: Yes (same 3-year rule)
  • Funding: Released in limited rounds; demand often exceeds funds within days

A 20% down payment assistance loan eliminates PMI, reduces your monthly payment significantly, and dramatically changes your purchasing power. You need to be ready to act when the funding window opens.

County and City Programs in Southern California

Beyond CalHFA, every major county and many cities in SoCal administer their own assistance programs — often stackable with CalHFA. Examples: LA County DCBA First-Time Homebuyer Program; City of LA LIPA; San Diego County and City Housing Commission programs; Riverside CalHome; San Bernardino County Housing Authority; Orange County city programs (Irvine, Anaheim, Santa Ana, etc.); Ventura County CHDO and city programs. Income and purchase price limits apply and vary by area.

Common Requirements

Most CalHFA and county programs share: first-time buyer (no owned/occupied primary in past 3 years); owner-occupancy (primary residence only); income limits by household size and county; purchase price limits; homebuyer education (approved course, often 8 hours online); and an approved lender. I am CalHFA-approved and work with these programs regularly. When you come to me as a first-time buyer, I run every available program against your situation before we decide on a structure.
